title: Lacy hexagon
subtitle: Open double-treble fans between six defined corners — airy enough for a shawl, structured enough for a panel
excerpt: The lacy hexagon replaces the side cluster groups with double trebles and chain-3 spaces, opening up the fabric between the six corners. Four rounds give a 13 cm point-to-point motif with six open sides and six defined corners — light enough for shawl work but with enough structure to hold its shape as a cushion panel.
sourceNotes: Weldon's Practical Crochet, Volumes 1-3 (1885-1890) — lace hexagonal motifs and filet construction (Internet Archive). Therese de Dillmont, Encyclopedia of Needlework (1886), crochet lace motif chapter.
heroPrompt: A lacy crochet hexagon in cream DK cotton on a pale linen background, photographed flat from above in soft daylight — the 13 cm motif shows six open chain-3 side spaces between six defined treble corner pairs, the lace structure visible through the open fabric.

crochet.gaugeText: Each finished four-round lacy hexagon measures 13 cm point-to-point in DK-weight cotton with a 4 mm hook, after steam-blocking.

chartDefinition.title: Lacy hexagon
chartDefinition.caption: Four rounds from the magic ring. Six corner ch-2 spaces hold standard (3tr, ch 2, 3tr) corner groups. Side spaces use double trebles and chain-3 spans from round 2, replacing solid clusters with open lace arches.

glossaryTerms.definition: UK double treble (dtr): yarn over twice, insert hook, pull up loop, [yarn over, pull through 2 loops] 3 times. Taller than a treble. Called triple crochet (trc) in US patterns.
The gap created by skipping a chain or chains. In the lacy hexagon, chain-3 spaces form the open arches between corner groups on the sides; chain-2 spaces hold the corner cluster pairs.
A chain space bridged by a tall stitch (typically a double treble) to create an open, airy side span between solid corner anchors. The defining visual element of the lacy hexagon.

content.text: The lacy hexagon opens up the side spaces between the six corners by replacing solid cluster groups with
double-treble
columns and
chain-space

arches. The six corners keep the same (3tr, ch 2, 3tr) construction as the basic hexagon; it is only the side spans that change. Four rounds give a 13 cm point-to-point motif — slightly larger than the standard hexagon because the open arches spread the fabric wider.
Each
lace-arch

on round 2 is a single double treble flanked by chain-3 spaces. Rounds 3 and 4 add more double trebles to each arch, building three spans per side by round 4. Blocking is important on this motif: the open arches need steam to settle flat and hold their shape.

attrs.title: Materials for one motif
attrs.body: About 7 g of DK-weight cotton. A 4 mm crochet hook (UK 8, US G/6). Tapestry needle. Scissors. A blocking mat and pins — lace hexagons need thorough pinning to hold the open arch shape.

content.text: Gauge

Each finished four-round lacy hexagon measures 13 cm point-to-point in DK-weight cotton with a 4 mm hook, after steam-blocking. The open construction means the pre-block measurement may be 1 to 2 cm smaller — always measure after blocking.
Stitches used
chain (ch) — UK and US shared.
slip stitch (sl st) — UK and US shared.
treble (tr) — UK; called double crochet (dc) in US patterns.
double treble (dtr) — UK; yarn over twice before inserting the hook. Called triple crochet (trc) in US patterns.
magic ring (MR) — adjustable starting loop; no centre hole.
Pattern
Worked in the round, right side facing throughout. Ch 3 at the start of each round counts as the first treble of the first corner cluster. Do not turn.
Round 1

Form a magic ring. Ch 3 (counts as first tr). Work 2 tr into the ring. *Ch 2, 3 tr into the ring*; repeat from * to * four more times. Ch 2, sl st to top of beg ch-3. Pull tail to close ring. (18 tr, 6 ch-2 corner spaces.)
Round 2

Sl st across next 2 tr and into first ch-2 corner sp. Ch 3. Into same sp work 2 tr, ch 2, 3 tr (corner made). *Ch 3, dtr into the gap between the two corner groups, ch 3. Into next ch-2 corner sp work (3 tr, ch 2, 3 tr)*; repeat from * to * four more times. Ch 3, dtr into the gap, ch 3. Sl st to top of beg ch-3. (18 corner tr, 6 dtr, 6 ch-2 corners, 12 ch-3 side spaces.)
Round 3

Sl st into first ch-2 corner sp. Ch 3. Into same sp work 2 tr, ch 2, 3 tr. *Ch 3, dtr into next ch-3 sp, ch 3, dtr into next dtr, ch 3, dtr into next ch-3 sp, ch 3. Into next ch-2 corner sp work (3 tr, ch 2, 3 tr)*; repeat from * to * four more times. Ch 3, dtr into next ch-3 sp, ch 3, dtr into next dtr, ch 3, dtr into next ch-3 sp, ch 3. Sl st to top of beg ch-3. (18 corner tr, 18 dtr, 6 ch-2 corners, 24 ch-3 side spaces.)
Round 4

Sl st into first ch-2 corner sp. Ch 3. Into same sp work 2 tr, ch 2, 3 tr. *Ch 3, [dtr into next ch-3 sp, ch 3] twice, dtr into next dtr, ch 3, [dtr into next ch-3 sp, ch 3] twice. Into next ch-2 corner sp work (3 tr, ch 2, 3 tr)*; repeat from * to * four more times. Ch 3, [dtr into next ch-3 sp, ch 3] twice, dtr into next dtr, ch 3, [dtr into next ch-3 sp, ch 3] twice. Sl st to top of beg ch-3. Fasten off. (18 corner tr, 30 dtr, 6 ch-2 corners, 36 ch-3 side spaces.)
Chart

The chart reads outward from the magic ring. Six corner ch-2 spaces anchor solid treble corner groups throughout; the open double-treble arches between corners grow from one dtr per side in round 2 to five per side in round 4.

definition.title: Lacy hexagon
definition.caption: Four rounds from the magic ring. Six corner ch-2 spaces anchor solid treble groups; double-treble lace arches with ch-3 spans fill the sides. Round 4 has five dtr per side edge.

content.text: Finishing

Fasten off, leaving a 15 cm tail. Weave through 3 to 4 stitches on the wrong side and trim. Weave in the magic ring tail. Block on a foam mat: pin all six corner points first, then ease each arch open and pin the centre of each chain-3 span to hold it in place. Apply steam and leave flat until fully dry.
Joining

The lacy hexagon joins at its six corner ch-2 spaces and along the open arch sides. For a flat seam, whip-stitch through the corresponding chain-3 spaces on adjacent motifs, taking the stitch through the chain rather than the post. The open construction means joins are less visible than in a solid cluster hexagon.
Care
Handwash in cool water. Do not tumble-dry. Lay flat and re-pin the six points while damp — the open lace arches will contract if left to dry unblocked and the motif will lose its shape.
What to try next

The lacy mandala uses the same double-treble fan construction but works outward in a circular shape rather than hexagonal, giving a shawl or wall-hanging centrepiece. The basic hexagon is the solid-cluster version of this motif — useful if you want to mix solid and lacy hexagons in the same blanket.
